_comment: The change ledger — the single source of truth for every versioned fact on this site. Topic pages embed a record with <div class="change" data-change="<id>">; deprecations.html, timeline.html and migrations.html are generated from these same records, so the ledger can never drift from the prose. Fields: since/deprecated/removed are major versions of `tool` (null = not applicable). `migration` is the exact command that automates the change, if one exists. `docs` are ids into links.json.

changes.title: Getting a dependency
changes.why: Works in functions and field initialisers, not just constructors — which is what makes functional guards, functional interceptors and reusable composables possible at all. It also drops the constructor boilerplate and plays better with inheritance.

changes.title: Declaring a component
changes.now: Standalone by default — no `standalone: true`, no NgModule
changes.was: standalone: true written explicitly (v15–18), or declared in an NgModule (pre-v15)
changes.why: NgModules existed to tell the compiler what a template could see. Standalone components carry their own `imports` array, so the indirection was pure overhead. v14 previewed it, v15 stabilised it, v19 made it the default and made the flag redundant.

changes.title: Conditionals and loops in a template
changes.why: Built-in syntax needs no imports, type-narrows properly inside the block, and lets the compiler generate far less code. @for also *requires* a track expression, which turns the most common Angular performance bug into a compile error.

code.was:
{{ u.name }}

Signed out
  • {{ item.label }}

changes.title: Holding reactive state
changes.was: A plain field plus manual change detection, or a BehaviorSubject you had to subscribe to
changes.why: Signals track their own readers, so Angular knows exactly which views depend on which state — that is the mechanism zoneless change detection is built on. They arrived in preview in v16 and stabilised in v20.

changes.title: Declaring an input
changes.now: input() / input.required() — a signal you read with ()
changes.why: A signal input is readable in computed() and effect() without a setter or ngOnChanges, and input.required() makes a missing input a compile-time error rather than an undefined at runtime.

changes.title: Declaring a service
changes.why: Root-provided was what almost every service wanted, so v22 made it the shape of the decorator rather than an option you configure. @Service() is auto-provided by default; pass { autoProvided: false } for a service that must be listed in a providers array, or { factory } to build it from a function.

changes.title: Running code at startup
changes.why: The token form needed multi: true and a factory, and forgetting either failed silently at runtime rather than at compile time. The provide* functions take the callback directly. The same swap applies to ENVIRONMENT_INITIALIZER and PLATFORM_INITIALIZER.

changes.title: Declaring an output
changes.why: An output is not a stream you subscribe to, so modelling it as an EventEmitter (an RxJS Subject) always promised more than it delivered. output() exposes only emit(), which is the entire API a component actually needs, and it cannot be accidentally subscribed to or completed.

changes.title: Referencing a child element or component
changes.was: @ViewChild() / @ContentChild() decorators, with a static flag and a lifecycle hook to wait for
changes.why: The decorator form set a plain property at some point during a lifecycle hook, so reading it too early gave you undefined and the fix was to know which hook. A signal query is just a signal: read it whenever, use it in computed(), and the timing question disappears along with the static flag.

changes.title: Loading part of a template lazily
changes.was: A route-level lazy load, or a manual dynamic import plus ViewContainerRef
changes.why: Lazy loading used to be something you could only do at a routing boundary. @defer moves it into the template, so a heavy chart or a rarely-opened dialog is split out of the bundle without restructuring the application around it. The dependencies used only inside the block go with it automatically.

changes.title: Naming a value inside a template
changes.was: *ngIf="expr as name", or a wrapper <ng-container> whose only job was to hold the alias
changes.why: Aliasing used to be a side effect of a structural directive, which meant you needed a conditional you did not want in order to name a value you did. Worse, *ngIf's alias silently dropped the block when the value was falsy — 0 and '' vanished. @let just declares a name.

changes.title: Unsubscribing in a component
changes.was: takeUntil(this.destroy$) with a manual Subject and ngOnDestroy
changes.why: No boilerplate Subject, no lifecycle hook to forget. It ties to DestroyRef, so it also works in services and functions — anywhere with an injection context — not just components.

changes.title: Default change detection strategy
changes.now: OnPush — applied automatically when changeDetection is not set
changes.was: Default (check-everything) unless you opted into ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush by hand
changes.why: The old default re-checked every binding in the tree on every event. OnPush was always the right answer for signal-based components, so v22 stopped making you ask for it.

changes.title: Building a form
changes.now: Signal Forms — form state as signals (stable in v22)
changes.why: Reactive forms predate signals, so form state lived in a parallel Observable world that never composed with the rest of a signal-based component. Signal Forms close that gap, and interop is deliberate: large reactive forms can migrate piece by piece rather than all at once.

changes.title: HttpClient's transport
changes.was: XMLHttpRequest by default; fetch opt-in via withFetch()
changes.why: fetch is the platform standard, works in more runtimes, and is what SSR needs. v22 flipped the default; a migration exists for anyone who still depends on XHR-specific behaviour.

changes.title: The unit test runner
changes.why: Karma drives a real browser per run and predates the Vite-based build pipeline Angular now uses; Vitest reuses that pipeline, so tests start in a fraction of the time. v21 shipped the unified builder and made Vitest the default for new projects. Karma still runs, but is deprecated and takes no new features.

changes.title: Turning an Observable into a Promise
changes.why: toPromise() was ambiguous about which value you wanted and resolved to undefined — silently — when the source completed empty. The replacements make the choice explicit and reject with EmptyError instead of handing you undefined.

changes.title: Retrying with a delay
changes.why: retryWhen exposed a notifier Observable that almost everybody used incorrectly — completing it silently stopped retrying, and errors in the notifier were easy to swallow. The config object covers the real use cases directly.

changes.title: Configuring a multi-package test setup
changes.now: The projects option inside the root config
changes.why: Two files described one thing. Folding projects into the root config removed a whole category of "which file wins?" confusion. Deprecated in 3.2, gone in 4.

changes.title: Running tests in a real browser
changes.now: Browser Mode (stable) with a provider package: @vitest/browser-playwright
changes.was: Experimental Browser Mode with the provider named as a string
changes.why: Browser Mode left experimental in v4, and providers moved into their own packages so you install only the driver you actually use rather than pulling every option into the dependency tree.

changes.title: Dependency install scripts
changes.now: Blocked by default; opt packages in explicitly
changes.why: A postinstall script is arbitrary code execution at install time, and the Rspack supply-chain attack used exactly that to ship a cryptominer. pnpm 10 turned it off by default. In v10 you allow-list with pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies; v11 replaced that whole family of settings with allowBuilds.

changes.title: Where pnpm settings live
changes.was: The pnpm field in package.json, and .npmrc
changes.why: pnpm's settings had been squatting in two files owned by other tools. v11 split them cleanly: .npmrc keeps registry and auth settings, everything pnpm-specific moves to YAML. Environment variables moved too — npm_config_* is no longer read, use pnpm_config_*.
